body:
Found by T217's review (2026-08-25): a caller holding a channel handle from before a sever
can call setChannel/sync-stamp paths after the drop, and the stamp writes a fresh operator-
signed channel record — the severed channel reappears in channelStatus with no pool behind
it. The drop's negation covered the OLD record; the re-stamp mints a new one.

Build: stamping refuses when the channel's record lineage is severed (the drop's negation
stands and no open has re-created the channel) — the refusal names the sever and the re-open
path. Rails: sever, then drive the stale handle's stamp — refused, channelStatus stays empty
(two-sided: a live channel's stamp still lands).

Acceptance criteria:
(a) A post-sever stamp through a stale handle refuses, naming the sever; channelStatus and
    channelsEver agree the channel is severed. Verify: new test in
    test/federation/curse-authority.test.ts or its own file.
(b) `loam federate open` after a sever still creates a fresh channel cleanly (the legitimate
    re-open is untouched). Verify: same file.

Merge tier: repair. Self-merge on the ordinary bar.
title: A stale handle can re-stamp a severed channel back into existence
